page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-32-lssd is an arm64-based server instance powered by a dedicated 32-core ARM Neoverse-V2 processor. Operating with one thread per physical core, the CPU features a cache configuration of 64 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 80 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For high-speed local storage, the instance includes 2412 GB of NVMe SSD capacity distributed across six local SSDs. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance, and it does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory subsystem performance, with a Passmark memory score in the top tier (top 10%) and read-only small block memory bandwidth reaching 3959.92 GB/sec. Large block read and write bandwidths are also strong at 345.42 GB/sec and 163.3 GB/sec respectively. Computational performance is solid, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance at 58106.37 and a Passmark CPU score of 29102.03, both falling in the average range. The instance demonstrates strong database capabilities, scoring in the top tier for Passmark database operations with 49685.86, and achieving a strong 69.35 million operations per second in Redis SET operations.

Given the combination of dedicated ARM cores, high memory bandwidth, and substantial local NVMe SSD storage, this instance is highly suited for database operations, high-throughput web serving, and data compression tasks. The presence of 2412 GB of local NVMe SSD storage makes it an efficient choice for workloads requiring low-latency storage access without the overhead of network-attached storage. While it lacks x86-specific instruction sets like AVX or AMX, its strong performance in database operations and memory-bound tasks offers a highly resource-dense profile for modern cloud-native applications.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-32-lssd is an arm64 server instance featuring 32 dedicated physical cores powered by the ARM Neoverse-V2 processor. It is configured with 128.0 GB of RAM (4.0 GB per core) and 2412 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The instance lacks GPU acceleration and x86-specific vector extensions but delivers top-tier memory performance, as evidenced by its top 10% Passmark memory score and strong memory bandwidth metrics. Benchmark results highlight its exceptional capability in database operations, scoring in the top tier for Passmark database tasks and achieving 69.35 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. With strong multi-threaded decompression and static web serving throughput, this instance is optimized for high-performance database deployments, web serving, and storage-intensive workloads requiring fast local I/O.
